st: Geoengineering, non-chemical trails and other bogeymen to get past

sec.t: ff.56.1 The last 22k years of the Earth's thermometer
sec.p: When in doubt, zoom out. Let's start with history. With prehistory, actually. It's always good to put concepts and trends in perspective. Take the warming of our planet. Here are recent estimates for the last 22 thousand years. The end of the ice age brought +4°C.

Agriculture raised atmospheric CO2 to 280ppm. Glacial cycles predicted 240ppm for pre-industrial levels. 6000 years ago the Earth's average temperature was 1 degree higher than in the 19th century and, without agriculture, Canada would have been covered in ice.

sec.t: ff.56.3 A waterfall one kilometre high
sec.p: Given the immense (solar) energy reaching the Earth, tiny variations (like the amount of reflected light) make geoengineering easy to implement. At the same time, they make the balance precarious.
Oliver Morton, a senior editor at The Economist (no small fry), published The Planet Remade, an excellent book on the subject.
Sure, but what about the costs? Direct air capture of CO2 is, for now, very complex and not very effective.
